survey: A wooden pier runs along the shoreline, seen from a high three-quarter view. Its left end rests on the sand, and the rest stands in shallow water. The deck is made of parallel planks on a side beam, carried by round piles. Front piles stand in front of the deck's edge beam and go down into the water. Back piles show under the deck and stand in the water. Several pile tops come up through the deck as short stubs, which is normal pier construction. A lifebuoy hangs from a peg on a tall front pile, near the middle. A rope is coiled closed around the pile near the right end, with no loose tail. A taller mooring pile stands by itself at the far right corner. Every pile goes into either water or sand, and the deck rests on them. The pier joins the shore at its left end.
